pairs.question: Quid tibi vis?
pairs.answer: Domine mi tu iurasti per Dominum Deum tuum ancillae tuae Salomon filius tuus regnabit post me et ipse sedebit in solio meo.
pairs.derivation: King David asks Bathsheba quid tibi vis (framing inquit dropped). Her reply opens quae respondens ait domine mi... — answer takes her first sentence stating his oath, ending at solio meo; what follows (et ecce nunc Adonias regnavit...) is further complaint, not the answer.

pairs.question: Pacificusne ingressus tuus?
pairs.derivation: Bathsheba asks Adonias whether his coming is peaceful (pacificusne ingressus tuus). He answers qui respondit pacificus; framing qui respondit dropped.

pairs.question: Tune es vir Dei qui venisti de Iuda?
pairs.derivation: The old prophet asks the man of God tune es vir Dei qui venisti de Iuda; he replies respondit ille ego sum, with framing respondit ille dropped.

pairs.question: Num tu es domine mi Helias?
pairs.derivation: Abdias asks num tu es domine mi Helias; reply cui ille respondit ego — framing cui ille respondit dropped, answer is the single word ego.

pairs.question: Tune es ille qui conturbas Israhel?
pairs.answer: Non turbavi Israhel sed tu et domus patris tui qui dereliquistis mandata Domini et secuti estis Baalim.
pairs.derivation: Ahab asks Elias tune es ille qui conturbas Israhel; Elias answers et ille ait non turbavi Israhel... (framing et ille ait dropped). Answer runs to the full stop after Baalim; the next verse (verumtamen nunc mitte...) turns to a command.

pairs.question: Per quem?
pairs.derivation: Ahab asks per quem (sc. shall the Lord deliver them). The reply dixitque ei haec dicit Dominus per pedisequos principum provinciarum answers per pedisequos principum provinciarum; the prophetic framing dixitque ei haec dicit Dominus is dropped.

pairs.question: Quis incipiet proeliari?
pairs.derivation: Ahab's second question quis incipiet proeliari is answered et ille dixit tu; framing et ille dixit dropped, answer is tu.
